newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia and insurers drive Helsinki to new records.
newsitem.headline: Nokia and insurers drive Helsinki to new records.

text.p: A Nokia-led rally and sharp gains in insurance stocks pushed shares to a new record close in lively trade on Thursday, brokers said.

The HEX general index closed at 2,903.18 -- its highest-ever close -- after setting a new 2,903.80 intra-session record in the afternoon. Trade was 811 million markka with over a third in bourse engine Nokia.

Nokia added 7.00 markka to close at 312.00 markka, matching an overnight correction higher on Wall Street. It hit 314.00 intra-day as the share continued to recover from a soft spell that followed its 1996 earnings report last week.
Brokers were mixed on the prospects for a sustained rally with some fearing strength could fade.
Insurer Sampo added 30.00 markka to close at 480.00 in heavy volume after first being bid up in small lots and with heavier dealings at the upper levels.
Rival Pohjola tracked Sampo, gaining 8.00 markka to 153.00 markka to help push the insurance sub-index almost six percent higher in hefty trade.
The shares were fuelled by continued expectations of more restructuring in Nordic banking and insurance after Swedish Foreningsbanken and Swedbank merged on Tuesday, brokers said.
"Some people think that something will have to happen in Finland soon," said one.
Forest industry group UPM-Kymmene rose 2.20 markka to close at 107.00 markka in heavy 90 million markka volume.
Pharmaceuticals group Orion ended at a 188.00 markka all-time high, up 4.00 in lively 28 million markka dealings ahead of its 1996 report due on Friday.
The median of forecasts was for a 739 million markka profit before extraordinary items, up from 670 million in 1995.
"The result is expected to be good," one broker said. Swedish Astra's strong report on Wednesday may have boosted interest in Nordic pharmaceuticals, said another.
